audit.whatIsWrong: EVEN / 6-10 fits 50.38% over 925 games; the stage split did not.
audit.why: The lane is a series of hand-offs: level 1 yours, 3 to 5 hers as Bladesurge resets stack her passive, level 6 even, first item hers, and a last window at two items.
audit.corrected: Kept the rating, restored the hand-offs in the chart.

audit.whatIsWrong: Rows 0, 1, 2, 3 and 5 contradicted the packet — and rows 2, 3 and 5 contradicted this entry's own whys, which hand those stages to Irelia.
audit.why: The mirror flipped rows 0, 2, 3 and 5 in matched pairs and set row 4 to 5/10; the packet chart (Olaf/Skill/Irelia/Irelia/Skill/Irelia/Olaf) agrees.
audit.corrected: Rows 0, 1, 2, 3 and 5 flipped as one atomic group in both layers; ratings 6/5/4/4/5/4.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three strings say Defiant Dance blocks or sponges Reckless Swing, and one says it heals her.
audit.why: Riot's Defiant Dance text is a charged strike that takes REDUCED PHYSICAL DAMAGE while charging — no healing at all, and no reduction on true damage. Reckless Swing goes through it in full. Her healing is Bladesurge, which also refreshes its own cooldown off a Marked target.
audit.corrected: Stated that Defiant Dance only cuts physical damage so Reckless Swing lands anyway, and moved the healing to Bladesurge.

audit.whatIsWrong: Four strings say Ragnarok 'cleanses' or 'strips' Flawless Duet's stun.
audit.why: Ragnarok grants immunity to disables only while he keeps attacking, on 100/90/80s; it removes nothing already applied. Flawless Duet is 16/14.5/13/11.5/10s, so she can hold it until your ultimate ends.
audit.corrected: Rewritten as disable immunity that holds while you swing, in whys[4], spikes[1], wants.you[2] and mid.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three strings give Olaf's W sustain or omnivamp.
audit.why: Tough It Out is attack speed plus a shield; the lifesteal is the passive and rises as his health falls — which is why the short-trade advice against Irelia needed the passive named, not the W.
audit.corrected: Split correctly in tradeGood, dosFull[1].d and mid.

audit.whatIsWrong: Flawless Duet's grounding flag is not used.
audit.why: The kit file tags it with grounding, but Riot's description says damaged, stunned and Marked only. Trust-the-description, so nothing here claims her E denies movement beyond the stun.

edits.before: This is her window and you have to respect it. From 3 to 5 she stacks her passive on your autos, Q-resets through the wave, and her W blocks your Reckless Swing burst while healing her back, so a long trade favors her — keep them short and let your W-omnivamp top you off. Everything flips at 6: Ragnarok strips her E-stun and CC entirely, so when you ult she can't peel and your true damage runs her down. Bait the E or wait it out, then ult and commit — that's your equalizer in a lane she otherwise edges.
edits.after: This is her window and you have to respect it. From 3 to 5 she stacks her passive on your autos and Bladesurges through the wave, healing on every reset, so a long trade favors her — keep them short and let your missing-health lifesteal top you off. Defiant Dance only cuts PHYSICAL damage, so Reckless Swing lands through it in full. Everything flips at 6: Ragnarok keeps you disable-immune while you keep attacking, so her stun cannot peel. Bait the E or wait it out, then ult and commit.

edits.before: The math turns on her at items but not in your favor — your flat Reckless Swing true damage and short axe fights lose value while her item spikes make every extended duel hers, and her W keeps blocking your one big nuke. You don't out-scale her, so don't try to win this lane at three items. Convert the level-6 Ragnarok dives and your early pressure into towers and objectives, then become the diver who ults past her peel onto their backline rather than the laner trying to 1v1 a scaled Irelia.
edits.after: The math turns on her at items but not in your favor — your flat Reckless Swing true damage and short axe fights lose value while her item spikes make every extended duel hers, and Bladesurge heals back what you chip. You don't out-scale her, so don't try to win this lane at three items. Convert the level-6 Ragnarok dives and your early pressure into towers and objectives, then become the diver who ults past her peel onto their backline instead of duelling a scaled Irelia.

notes: Best find here: three strings told the reader Defiant Dance blocks Reckless Swing. Riot's text reduces PHYSICAL damage only, so Olaf's true damage lands through it in full — the old advice was telling a player to hold the one ability that beats her W. Defiant Dance also does not heal; Bladesurge does, and it refreshes on a Marked target. Chart rows 0, 1, 2, 3 and 5 flipped to the packet and the mirror; rows 2, 3 and 5 previously said Olaf while the whys under them said Irelia.
